summary:
Nothing is broken, but one finding is still open. A warp gate added to a system that has a ground base now gets a different anchor id than before the landing work (257 of 257 systems with a base), so the id a peer stored for such a gate now names the base. The fix is not small and I did not make it. The open finding has an it.fails test, as does the zone gap described under hysteresis. Also unverified: I never built a ram that pushes a ship down into the ground, I did not run the mission/respawn paths through a browser, and the browser run did not fly a landing.

Final state: tsc is clean for all three packages; vitest passes 587 tests plus 2 expected failures (the open findings), against the 542 baseline; the browser run (build, empty .data, node scripts/e2e.mjs) ended "e2e ok" after my server changes.

I fixed nine findings. Each has a test that failed on the code as I found it, and the failing output is saved in the scratchpad.

Two fixes are gameplay rule changes you did not ask for and should confirm. First, a ship can no longer dock at a base with terrain between it and the pad. Second, empty wrecks are now evicted before loaded ones.

The ground-impact charge rule changed. What a ship has paid for earlier impacts now fades over 1 s, instead of one flat charge per second-long episode.

The review of the three items the second core engineer named:
- One-second impact episode: it let a ship slam repeatedly for the first slam's price. Fixed.
- Ray stepping: it missed far more than a thin ridge. Fixed.
- Events to the whole shell: they leaked positions of far-away ships. Fixed for events that carry a position.

Task items 1 to 9:
1. Determinism: held.
2. Frame conversions: held. Orbit energy drifts in the turning frame, within bounds.
3. Rule leaks: held. Cruise limits are lowered by a landable body's ceiling term, not leaked to other bodies.
4. Exploits: logout and landed-ship hits held. Crash-for-bounty, wreck-flush, saved-state and dock-through-a-hill were real and are fixed. The zone gap is open.
5. Objects on the ground: held.
6. Bases: held apart from dock-through-a-hill, which is fixed. Pads are flat everywhere.
7. Generator: bodies and sites identical; gate ids are the open finding.
8. NPCs in surface frames: held. Details under 'behaviour'.
9. Tick cost: 20 pilots near the ground cost 0.28 ms median against 0.24 ms at a station, so the ground path adds about 20%.
done: (a) LAND_MAX_SLOPE = 0.36397023426620234 and LAND_MIN_UPRIGHT = 0.8660254037844387 are literals in packages/shared/src/sim/ship.ts and exported. The degree constants stay. Test: tests/review-shell.test.ts.

(b) Orbital sites stay outside the surface-frame shell. Tested over 105,789 site/landable-body pairs in 2,880 systems, including the planet's moons and three gates per system. Every pair was proven apart by orbit ranges and none needed sampling. Least margin 11.7 km above the exit height; 10.1 km in a wider script run over 38,400 systems. Nothing in the generator enforces it, so the test pins it.

(c1) Impact episode: it let a ship slam repeatedly at the same speed for the price of the first slam. Fixed in packages/server/src/sim.ts and ground.ts: what has been paid now fades over IMPACT_EPISODE = 1 s, so a scrape costs about once and repeated slams cost again.

(c2) Ray stepping: groundRay missed 80% of ground hits for shots fired low and along the ground, because the 48-step cap ran out. Fixed: 24 to 250 m steps, at most 128. It now misses 0.4% of hits (measured), and a thin ridge in about 1 case in 20.

(c3) Events: every pilot in a surface zone received every event of the whole shell, including a hit with a ship's id and position 700 km away. Fixed: events with a position now go only to pilots within ZONE_VIEW_RADIUS.

Saved landed ships: a ship saved 80 m under the ground, 3 m under it or 60 m above it was restored as it was and stayed there, because a landed ship never samples the terrain. Fixed with reseatLanded in ground.ts, called from World.place: it comes back in flight, at rest.

Dock through a hill: docking only checked distance. 4.2% of low approach spots 700 to 1,700 m out had terrain between ship and pad. Fixed in modules/core.ts: a clear line to a point 60 m above the pad is required.

Crash on purpose to keep a bounty: a wanted pilot under fire could crash to deny the hunter bounty and kill. Fixed: a crash within 15 s of a weapon attack is credited to the attacker. A first version used lastHitBy and would have framed a bystander after a collision; a test caught it and it now uses new lastAttackedBy/At fields set in onAttack.
Wreck flush: twelve crashed free starter ships pushed a loaded wreck out of the 12-wreck cap, in a zone that covers a whole moon. Fixed in salvage.ts: empty wrecks are evicted first.

Ticket arrival: acceptTicket accepted any existing site id as a gate, so a sender-signed ticket could name a station or a ground base. Fixed in world.ts: the site must be of kind gate. A positive control with a real gate passes the check.

Held, with tests: cargo conservation, one deductible, and salvage worth less than the deductible after a crash; double destruction leaves one wreck; objects at rest on slope, pad, pad edge, blend ring and crater rim over 4,600 ticks; pods thrown fast over a ridge; undock and dock with a pad full of landed ships at six times of day; a ship at another landable body cannot dock here; logout removes a landed ship exactly as a flying one.
Tools in tests/tools/ (not part of vitest): compare-old-new.mts, terrain-browser.mjs with determinism-suite.ts, bench-tick.mts, ray-variants.mts, detection-ranges.mts, shell-search.mts.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md updated where the fixes made it untrue.
notDone: OPEN, owner decision: gate ids. A gate added later gets SITE_ID_BASE + sites.length, which now includes the bases, so a gate's id shifts by one per base. The gate project's stored p.site, the peer's stored remoteSite and any saved anchor near a gate then name a base. Test: tests/review-generator.test.ts, it.fails. A fix means non-dense ids, for example bases in a separate id range and gates counting only non-base sites. It touches several tests of other engineers (gates.test, generate.test, bases.test), so I did not do it.

OPEN, low: the zone hysteresis band. Between 300 km (enter) and 390 km (exit) a ship that came from above is in the body's frame and one that came from below is in the surface frame, so two ships side by side are in different zones. Test: it.fails in tests/review-landing.test.ts, which shows the zones differ (6 against 506). That they are mutually invisible and unhittable I concluded from the zone code, not by firing at one.

Not constructed: a ram that pushes the rammer down into the ground. In my ram test the rammer is 6 m above the landed ship's centre line, so it is pushed up, and the deepest tick-end position was 0.00 m under. A landed ship on a rise with the rammer downhill is the case I did not build.

Not tried: Firefox and WebKit (Playwright has only Chromium installed). Node and Chromium are both V8 (12.4 and a much newer one), so agreement shows only that two V8 versions, minified and optimised code, and Node without JIT all agree.

Not run in a browser: landing in the fixed universe or through the e2e script; mission hand-in and respawn at a base; night-side respawn. The respawn path is server code and the undock test covers six times of day over 24 h, which is not a full day of that moon.

Not measured: tick time with many beams or shots near the ground after the groundRay change (worst case about 134 terrain samples per trace; the bench has no firing ships), and cost of many objects in a surface zone.

Not tested empirically: the 400-event cap per zone per snapshot period. Reaching it needs several hundred events per 2 ticks, which I judged unreachable without checking. Local chat in a surface zone still reaches everyone around the moon, which I left as it is.

Not tried as attacks: landed ships being hit and unable to fire. These rest on the first-core and second-core engineers' tests in tests/landing.test.ts, which I read and ran, not on new attacks. The NPC-removal-per-pursuit case (an NPC removed when it follows a pilot below the frame height) was reasoned from the code, not run.
verification:
Run on the final tree. Files I touched or added (the checkpoint job committed them; I did not):
- packages/shared/src/sim/ship.ts
- packages/server: sim.ts, ground.ts, world.ts, game.ts, modules/core.ts, modules/salvage.ts, modules/combat/law.ts
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- tests/review-*.test.ts and tests/tools/*

Checks: `npx tsc -p packages/shared && npx tsc -p packages/server && npx tsc -p packages/client` is clean. `npx vitest run`: 38 files, 587 passed, 2 expected failures (the two it.fails). Ten earlier runs of the full suite or parts were stable, including two full-suite repeats. Ports 8420 and 8421 had no listener before the browser run. After it, netstat showed only closing connections on 8421.

Browser run: npm run build, rm -rf .data, node scripts/e2e.mjs ended "e2e ok", exit 0, after my server changes. Landing was not flown in it.

Per finding, the test failed before the fix; the output is in the scratchpad (impact episode, events and saved states, dock, crash and wreck, rays, ticket, frame-up).

1. Determinism (tests/tools/terrain-browser.mjs):
- The suite is bundled with Vite in library mode and minified (68 KB) and run in headless Chromium 158 and in Node 22.14 (V8 12.4).
- It covers 5 bodies: rocky, ice, desert, rocky with a pad and ice with a pad. Each gets 320 directions, half near the pad, at detail 0 to 3, plus sample tone, normal, relief and min/max, cold and after 150,000 warm-up calls.
- It also covers 4 landing flights through simulateShip. Two of them touched down; the other two stayed in flight for 4,000 ticks.
- 35,592 float64 values compared as bit patterns: 0 differ between Node and Chromium, 0 between cold and warm, and 0 between Node and node --jitless.
- Terrain.ts uses Math.sqrt, abs, floor, imul, min and max; Math.sin appears only in a comment. Math.hypot (v3.len and dist, addPull in gravity), Math.exp, Math.pow and Math.tan/cos in math.ts are used in flight, so full-flight bit identity across engines is not claimed.

2. Frame conversions (tests/review-frames.test.ts):
- On the 4 h-day fixture planet, falling in and climbing out across the border are each one crossing.
- Planet-centred error: position at most 2.3e-10 m, velocity at most 6.9e-13 m/s, orientation at most 1.5e-16 rad. The barycentric errors are 0 or 2e-13, but barycentric float resolution is about 3e-5 m, so I report the planet-centred numbers.
- Orbit at 100 km for 4 revolutions (667,600 ticks, about 6 h): relative energy change 2.5e-4 in the surface frame against 6e-7 in the frame that does not turn, and the positions end 11.9 km apart. The drift comes from integrating the Coriolis term explicitly and scales with the square of the spin rate. The shortest day of any landable body in 38,400 generated systems is 8.00 h, which is 4 times slower than the fixture. I did not change the integrator.

3. Compare against 546c1e1 (extracted with git archive into the scratchpad, imported by relative path, tests/tools/compare-old-new.mts):
- 8,933 scripted flights (about 400 to 900 ticks each), all identical tick by tick; I only counted scene kinds, so I give no ticks total. The tally by kind: stars (M 1,270 plus cruise 54, K 502, G 278, F 232, A 216, WD 194, NS 172, BH 149 plus cruise 57), gas giants 1,207, ice giants 578, atmosphere planets of many kinds, 431 beacons, 226 outposts, 141 stations, and 57 cruise flights at black holes.
- The black-hole figure counts the 149 normal and 57 cruise flights; the other kinds are listed in the tool's output.
- Cruise was flown only in the 186 systems with no landable body; the 1,062 systems with one got normal flight only.
- 1,248 systems for the generator comparison.
- Cruise limits changed at 2,820 sampled points (largest change 2.82 km/s, 0.13% of the old limit, never raised). All of them are exactly the landable ceiling term (0 deviations from the intended rule), which lowers the limit anywhere that term is binding.

4 and 5. Exploits and objects: see 'done'.

6. Bases (tests/review-bases.test.ts), 27 bases in the four named sectors and 260 more in 20 sectors:
- Slope on the pad: 0 degrees everywhere.
- Worst slope in the blend ring around it: 27.2 degrees in the four sectors, 33.9 degrees in the larger sample.
- Largest height step from pad level to the outer edge of the ring: 48.2 m. Largest cut or fill at the pad edge: 28.9 m.
- No pad is on a slope or in a crater wall beyond that; the ring is steeper than the 20 degree landing limit in places and under 45 degrees. A test pins these.

7. Generator: bodies and sites are identical for all 1,248 systems once bases are left out. The gate id shift is the open finding.

8. NPCs never enter a surface frame, because:
- spawnNpc throws for a surface zone;
- its only caller spawns where a site has a quota;
- the frame begins at most 300 km up and a station orbits at least 400 km up, against a 15 km NPC leash;
- NPC targeting needs the same anchor, so pursuit stops at the border;
- the tick removes an NPC that does get there.
Over 3,000 ticks with pilots at a station and a ring field, no NPC was ever in a surface frame and none was removed.

Stealth numbers: a landed Wisp is seen at 5.2 km and landed with silent running at 2.1 km, against 10.4 km flying idle and 4.2 km flying silent (tests/tools/detection-ranges.mts). Landing halves the detection range; whether that is intended is yours to decide.

9. Tick cost (tests/tools/bench-tick.mts, median over 900 ticks after warm-up, with a 33.3 ms budget):
- 1 pilot at the station: 0.088 ms.
- 20 pilots at the station: 0.237 ms, p95 0.335 ms.
- 20 pilots hovering 5 m over the ground, all in the surface frame so the terrain is sampled for each ship every tick: 0.284 ms, p95 0.423 ms.
- 5 NPC ships were in the system throughout (a station pilot was kept in all three runs).
The bench did not include firing ships.
requests: OWNER: decide the gate-id problem before any universe with warp gates upgrades. Option: give ground bases ids in a separate range so gates keep SITE_ID_BASE + non-base site count. Until then a stale stored gate id now gets a pilot refused at the arrival check (it was previously accepted anywhere), which beats being placed at a base.

OWNER: confirm two rule changes. (1) Docking at a base now needs a clear line to 60 m above the pad (new refusal 'No clear approach: the terrain is in the way.'). (2) Empty wrecks are evicted before loaded ones.
HUD ENGINEER: the dock prompt still shows within 1,750 m of a base where the server may now refuse for terrain; handle that refusal text.

OWNER, optional: the Coriolis term is integrated explicitly. If planets with day lengths under 8 h are ever generated, or accuracy over hours matters, switch to an exact rotation of the velocity. Today's worst generated case drifts about 6e-5 per 6 h of orbit.

OWNER, optional: the generator accepts a planet as a station host at 350 km altitude while the surface frame ends at 390 km for large planets, and relies on the 400 km minimum plus not being Hill-clipped. In 38,400 systems the least margin was 10.1 km. The new test will fail if a generator or constant change closes it.
BROWSER ENGINEER: a landing flight in universe 16 and the ground-base dock prompt are still unrun in a browser.
behaviour:
Rules as they are now:
- Landing limits: slope 0.36397023426620234 (tan 20 deg), upright 0.8660254037844387 (cos 30 deg), as exported literals.
- Hard landings: share of hull lost = 0.25 * (v / 10)^1.5 * hull scale, as before. What earlier impacts have cost fades with a 1 s time constant, and a contact pays only what it adds. For example, 14 m/s slams every 0.5 s now cost about 40% of the first one each.
- Crash credit: a ship destroyed by the ground within 15 s of another ship's weapon attack counts as destroyed by it; collisions do not count (the lastAttackedBy/At fields are set in law.onAttack).
- Shot ray: steps of half the height above the ground, clamped to 24..250 m, at most 128, plus 6 refinement halvings; nothing is sampled when the whole segment is above the body's highest ground.
- Events with a position (shot, hit, destroyed, mine, salvage, cruise, fold) in a surface zone go only to pilots within 120,000 m of the position; events without one still go to everyone in the zone.
- Dock at a base: also needs groundRay from the ship to a point 60 m above the pad to find no terrain; otherwise 'No clear approach: the terrain is in the way.'
- Saved landed ship: kept only if |altitude - belly| <= 0.5 m; otherwise Normal mode, velocity zero, raised onto the ground if it was under it.
- Wreck cap 12 per zone: wrecks with nothing left in them go first, then the oldest.
- Transfer ticket with arrival kind 'gate': the site must exist and be of kind gate.
- Surface-frame shell (b): least margin of a site periapsis over the exit height is 11.7 km in 2,880 systems and 10.1 km in 38,400.
names: packages/server/src/ground.ts: reseatLanded(state, def, belly); CRASH_CREDIT_SECONDS = 15; IMPACT_EPISODE now a memory time constant; RAY_STEPS 128, RAY_STEP_MIN 24.
packages/server/src/game.ts: Ship.lastAttackedBy, Ship.lastAttackedAt (set in combat/law.onAttack; read by SystemSim.groundImpact).
tests/review-shell.test.ts, review-frames.test.ts, review-bases.test.ts, review-generator.test.ts, review-landing.test.ts, review-rays.test.ts, review-ticket.test.ts: the review tests.

tests/tools/compare-old-new.mts (needs OLD_ROOT pointing at an extracted 546c1e1 and node_modules next to it), terrain-browser.mjs and determinism-suite.ts, bench-tick.mts, ray-variants.mts, detection-ranges.mts, shell-search.mts: run with npx tsx.
